title: Give the Mark III the hoe: a till action, a bare-soil channel and a 0.1 reward
tier_reason: Sim code behind the unit suite and the demo's gate; git reverts it. The values are the CEO's ruling, so nothing here is a taste call.
ask: Q-99, ruled 2026-09-09: a fresh Mark III on open ground random-walks off the field before earning anything. The CEO's fix, in his words: 'define an additional reward of 0.1 for hoeing a field and give the bot the option to till the soil. Then the bot would have more opportunities to do something beneficial by accident and then proceed to do something beneficial ongoingly.' Spec is WI-8 in docs/V0_2_1_PLAN.md.
first_action: After the night-rule fix has merged: add the bare channel to Observation.spec_default, tilled_tile 0.1 to Rewards.TABLE, action 5 = till here in BotBrain (wait becomes 6, weights sized for 7 actions), score it in on_result; move the demo's staging back to open ground and keep the gate as it is; update test_observation, test_policy sizes, test_learning_robot_day and the plan's section 9.
source_message: CEO on Q-99, 2026-09-09, chief of staff session.
result: Landed on main (commit 29bd672 merged): the bare-soil channel (128 inputs), tilled_tile 0.1, action 5 = till here (seven actions), scored in on_result; the demo back on open ground with the 24-farm harness. Fixed seed: days 1-3 average 3.1, days 5-7 6.5. 24 farms: learning 3.8 to 5.4, 22 of 24 weeks rose; control 3.7 to 4.6 (the field itself improves as the robot opens soil). Of earning waterings, 5.1 a day on its own opened soil, 0.0 on her sown block. LEARN_RATE moved 0.03 to 0.12 to pass the one-seed gate, which the worker flagged as luck. Unit 2366, integration 671, robot session and gateway green. Follow-ups queued: a multi-seed gate that asserts learning beats no learning; till limited to bare soil in the brain, the same rule the router applies to her, so it cannot hoe her wheat. Follow-up landed (commit c513be7 merged as 3fb65c4): the hoe now asks the same tool table her tap is resolved through, so a till on sown or growing soil is a spent decision — measured before the fix at 0.8 crop squares hoed per robot-week, plus 891 wasted strokes on already-open soil and 127 on the yard per 24 farm-weeks, now free. The one-seed gate is replaced by eight fixed farms, learning 5.91 against 5.40 squares a day on days 5-7, all eight above their own first three days, 8 seconds headless; LEARN_RATE settled at 0.06 from a 24-farm sweep. The price experiment the CEO made moot showed that paying less for the robot's own soil never sends it to a sown field. Unit 2374, integration 671, robot session and gateway green.

follow_ups.title: Choose the robot's learning speed from many farms, not one
follow_ups.first_action: Sweep LEARN_RATE across the 24-farm demo (candidates 0.03/0.06/0.12/0.24), report mean day-7 earnings and spread per value, and set the value that wins on the median farm rather than the one that passed the single fixed seed.
follow_ups.why: 0.12 was chosen to clear a one-seed check and the worker who chose it called it luck.

follow_ups.title: Stop the robot from hoeing the player's planted tiles
follow_ups.first_action: In the Mark III brain, mask action 5 (till) to bare-soil tiles only, matching the rule action_router already enforces for the player, and add a sim test that a tilled action on a sown tile is never emitted.
follow_ups.why: The brain can currently till a planted tile and destroy her wheat; only the router knows the rule.

follow_ups.title: Add a test that a learning robot out-earns one that never learns
follow_ups.first_action: Add a unit test running the 24-farm comparison over several seeds and asserting the learning cohort's week-7 mean exceeds the no-learning control by a stated margin, so a tuning change that only helps one seed fails.
follow_ups.why: The current check passes on a single seed, and the control farm improves on its own, so the margin is easy to fake.

follow_ups.title: Decide whether the robot should tend her crops or only its own soil
follow_ups.first_action: Draft a decision card in hq/data/decisions/ with the 5.1-vs-0.0 watering split, two options (leave the reward as is and let the robot farm its own plot, or add reward for watering player-sown tiles), and a recommendation, then open the matching Q-item in docs/DESIGNER_QUEUE.md.
follow_ups.why: The robot learned to farm beside her and never for her, which is a design direction only the CEO settles.

recommend.question: Ship v0.2.1 with a learning speed picked from one farm, or re-pick it from all 24 first?
recommend.answer: Accept the hoe now and have Kenji re-pick the number before the v0.2.1 tag.
recommend.why: A learning speed chosen because one seed happened to pass is not evidence the robot learns, and re-deriving it costs a demo run.
recommend.instead: Hold acceptance until the sweep is done — safer on paper, but the behaviour is already on main and green, so it delays the card without changing the code.
